newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks extend last week's gains.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks extend last week's gains.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rose Monday with investors in a festive mood after the Dow Jones industrial average last week soared 180 points amid a renewed slide in long-term interest rates.

At 1 p.m. EST, the 30-stock Dow index was up 15.00 points at 6,499.40, coming out of the strongest week since the first full week of November, when blue chips began a scorching month-long rally of more than 500 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 12-10 on subdued volume of 192 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said the market was again boosted by strength in bonds, but the trading pace slowed ahead of the Christmas holiday on Wednesday.

"It's a lackluster, pre-holiday market that is likely to be characterised by light volume," said Alan Ackerman, senior vice president and market strategist for Fahnestock & Co. "There's a bit of bargain hunting going on."
In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 10/32, lowering its yield, which moves in the opposite direction, to 6.58 percent from 6.61 percent at Friday's close.

"Considering the run-up last week, the market is holding itself in rather impressive form," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. "We've got a lot of random noise in the market in the days right before Christmas."
"It certainly has to be some solace to bulls that the market hasn't given up ground here," he said.
Strategists noted that the market was characterised by a reluctance by sellers to take profits.
The stocks of some computer makers were flagging, apparently on speculation that sales of personal computers were being helped only because of huge price cuts and special promotions.
Compaq Computer dropped 2-1/2 to 74-1/4, Dell fell 2-1/4 to 52-3/4, Gateway 2000 declined 2-5/8 to 54-3/4, and International Business Machines was off 3/8 to 154-1/8.
Pacific Gas shed 1-1/4 to 21-3/4 after Smith Barney reduced its rating on the stock.
W.R. Grace rose 1-3/4 to 50-3/8 on news that the company planned to sell its cocoa business to Archer Daniels for $430 million.
Alliant TechSystems fell 2 to 52-1/2 after the company said it was selling its Marine Systems business to Hughes Electronics for $141 million in cash.
The Nasdaq index was off 4.45 points at 1,284.11. The American Stock Exchange index lost 1.12 to 580.89.
